companies.name: ABB
companies.tagline: The medium-voltage innovator — HiPerGuard static MV UPS to 34.5 kV, 62 VoltaGrid flywheel condensers; Electrification orders +60% with triple-digit DC growth.

companies.name: American Electric Power
companies.tagline: The holding company that converted large-load demand into signed contract before anyone else at scale — 69 GW of incremental load by 2030 under executed service agreements across eleven states and three RTOs, eight commission-approved large-load tariffs, the country's largest transmission system and nearly 90 percent of its 765 kV network, and a $72B plan built on the physics of moving power at the highest voltage in North America.

companies.name: Aligned Data Centers
companies.tagline: The record $40B exit — AIP/MGX/GIP bought the 51-campus, 6.4 GW Americas platform from Macquarie with Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI inside the buyer consortium; patented Delta³/DeltaFlow waterless cooling (600+ kW/rack hybrid) is the moat.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.tagline: ~$220B capex and the #1 corporate clean-energy buyer — the Talen nuclear PPA set the FERC precedent; Trainium GW commitments anchor demand.

companies.name: Apex Clean Energy
companies.tagline: Wind-heritage farmdown IPP under Ares — 12 GW commercialized, 3+ GW operating/under construction, $4.08B financed in 2025; all three operating ERCOT batteries are Powin (bankrupt) and the next award went to Canadian Solar e-STORAGE — an open, FEOC-constrained storage buyer with no data-center customer yet.

companies.name: Applied Digital
companies.tagline: The AI-factory landlord — 1.4 GW / ~$36B leased to CoreWeave and one unnamed IG hyperscaler; PUE 1.18 waterless North Dakota design; 12.75% Macquarie preferred funds the build.

companies.name: Arevon Energy
companies.tagline: The Tesla-locked CAISO machine — seven-for-seven Megapack across ~5.6 GWh, pension-owned (APG/CalSTRS), transferability pioneer ($191M JPMorgan first), and an on-record domestic-supply doctrine.

companies.name: Bechtel
companies.tagline: The megaproject dynasty — ENR #2 at $19.5B with a $58.2B backlog; the only EPC to bring 21st-century US nuclear online, three concurrent LNG megatrains, and NVIDIA's partner for modularized gigawatt AI factories.

companies.name: Black & Veatch
companies.tagline: The interconnection specialist — client-owned substations that halve hyperscale grid timelines; ENR #6 Power + #8 Water + #1 Hydrogen (ACES Delta), and an equal seat in one of the first US SMR design-build JVs.

companies.name: Blattner
companies.tagline: The invisible fifth of US renewables — 75,000+ MW, 3,300+ storage containers and 5.4+ GWh built with near-zero disclosure; Quanta's renewables engine, owner-furnished batteries, and the Slate precedent of installing China-linked BESS.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.tagline: Sells time, not electrons — 55-day fuel-cell deployments beat the grid queue; Oracle up to 2.8 GW, AEP 1 GW firm; the scandium question is unresolved.

companies.name: Burns & McDonnell
companies.tagline: ENR's #1 power design firm eleven years running — the largest US substation design group and a claimed >50% RICE share, fused to Tier-3 data-center design-build under a 100% ESOP.

companies.name: BYD
companies.tagline: Blade LFP cells and gigascale BESS (HaoHan, MC Cube-T) — #1 in 2025 BESS system shipments per Benchmark; ranking scope-dependent.

companies.name: Canadian Solar (e-STORAGE)
companies.tagline: e-STORAGE's SolBank maker — NASDAQ-listed with a 75.1%-restructured CS PowerTech for FEOC compliance, a 2.5 GWh US data-center-demand order, and the unconfirmed Shelbyville KY ramp as the biggest swing factor.

companies.name: Caterpillar
companies.tagline: The gen-set OEM the AI buildout runs on — ~18% of the data-center generator market and 33% of tracked behind-the-meter capacity with Solar Turbines; a $72.1B backlog with diesel sets sold into 2028 and gas prime into 2029, Power Generation sales +38% in FY2025, large-engine capacity heading to ~3x 2024.

companies.name: CATL
companies.tagline: World's largest battery maker; TENER storage line — #1 in ESS cells five years running, with the lead narrowing per third-party estimates.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.tagline: The nuclear-PPA franchise — TMI/Crane restart 2027 for Microsoft, Meta's 1,121 MW Clinton deal, Calpine's $16.4B merger → 55 GW; §45U floors the downside.

companies.name: Core Scientific
companies.tagline: The shareholder-revolt vindication — rejected CoreWeave's $9B, then signed AMD for ~530 MW / $14B+; first miner-pivot with two 500 MW-class anchors, $24B+ backlog.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.tagline: The neocloud proxy — 1 GW+ active power, $99.4B backlog; GPU-backed debt repriced from 15% to investment grade; leased-power fragility on display.

companies.name: CRRC Zhuzhou Institute
companies.tagline: The rail SOE that became a top-tier BESS integrator — 1260H-listed, Hithium's ≥120 GWh anchor customer, and the CNY 0.46-0.53/Wh price-benchmark setter of Chinese grid tenders.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.tagline: The energy-first AI factory builder — Abilene 1.2 GW for OpenAI/Oracle, ~4.9 GW contracted of a 40+ GW pipeline; the deepest private-developer energy stack.

companies.name: Cummins
companies.tagline: Number-two data-center gen-set OEM; Power Systems spans engines, alternators, paralleling switchgear and battery storage

companies.name: Delta Electronics
companies.tagline: Volume leader in AI server power — AI data-center power and cooling crossed 50% of revenue; the deepest published 800 VDC stack; Megmeet contests the sidecar.

companies.name: Dominion Energy
companies.tagline: Data Center Alley's regulated gatekeeper — ~53.8 GW of data-center capacity contracted at July 2026 (12.0 GW firm) against a 24.7 GW peak, a GS-5 large-load class with 14-year terms and 85%/60% minimums from January 2027, a $64.7B plan that is a quarter transmission, and an agreed all-stock sale to NextEra Energy closing in late 2027.

companies.name: DPR Construction
companies.tagline: The technical builder of Stargate Abilene — self-performing GC with ~6,000 craft workers and prefab on 90%+ of new work; ENR #7 at $14.0B with $26.1B of new contracts booked.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.tagline: Grid-to-chip by acquisition — ~$12.5B for Fibrebond, Boyd Thermal, Ultra PCS; DC orders +240%; we assess content-per-MW gain, not unit-share capture.

companies.name: ERock (Enchanted Rock)
companies.tagline: Public gas-microgrid platform (NYSE: EROC) — Microsoft, Meta/EPE, and a 470 MW Anthropic order; the archetype FEOC-immune AIDC bridge/backup vendor with no BESS in the product

companies.name: Entergy
companies.tagline: The utility that certifies generation for one named hyperscaler at a time — 2,262 MW approved in Louisiana for Meta in 2025 and 5,278 MW more filed for its second phase, three 754 MW plants pre-certified in Mississippi for AWS, solar-plus-storage and gas in Arkansas for Google — inside MISO South, under five regulators and three formula rate plans, on a turbine exclusivity agreement raised to 27 power islands and a $67B plan.

companies.name: Envision Energy
companies.tagline: The other NDAA §154-named major — WoodMac tied-#5 integrator whose AESC cells arm Fluence and Prevalon via the Fixx template, with the strongest (China-proven) AIDC storyline in the field.

companies.name: Eolian
companies.tagline: The American-built ideologue and energy-plus-load pioneer — CyrusOne DFW7 monetizes a BESS interconnection, Flint Grid is PJM's largest battery in the Columbus AI corridor, and both GWh-class supplier slots are open (to FEOC-clean vendors).

companies.name: Equinix
companies.tagline: The interconnection incumbent building bolder — xScale >$15B JV for hyperscale, >100 MW of Bloom fuel cells, four nuclear agreements; Q2 2026 beat-and-raise.

companies.name: EVE Energy
companies.tagline: #3 global ESS cells and the 628Ah pioneer (Mr.Big/Mr.Giant) — first grid-connected 600Ah+ station; AI-rack BBU push; DoD listing and LG's ITC suit are the US clouds.

companies.name: Flex
companies.tagline: Contract manufacturer that bought its way into owning the data-centre power train — Anord Mardix, Crown, JetCool, EP² and a .4bn EPC Power deal — then approved spinning the whole segment out for early 2027.

companies.name: FlexGen
companies.tagline: Software-first US BESS integrator (HybridOS EMS) — assessed as a services-lane specialist after acquiring Powin's assets in 2025.

companies.name: Fluence
companies.tagline: Global storage integrator — Smartstack/Gridstack with Mosaic/Nispera software; US domestic-content supply chain and a $6.4B backlog.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.tagline: Holds the scarcest assets — turbine slots selling for 2031 delivery, Prolec transformer capacity; the time-to-power toll booth; wind still subtracts.

companies.name: Google
companies.tagline: The most storage-forward hyperscaler — owns Intersect Power, backs Form Energy iron-air, runs 1 GW demand response; TPU v7 now sells externally.

companies.name: Hitachi Energy
companies.tagline: World's largest transformer maker and HVDC leader — $57.9B backlog, 30-40 month lead times, $9B+ capacity program; its calendar is everyone's constraint.

companies.name: Hithium
companies.tagline: Stationary-only LFP cell and BESS specialist — Top-2 2025 ESS cell shipments; now fielding a four-SKU lithium-sodium AIDC line (zero named customers yet); financing remains the primary watch item

companies.name: HITT Contracting
companies.tagline: America's #1 data-center builder by revenue — $13B on an 82% mission-critical mix, 2+ GW commissioned; the 180-day 22.5 MW speed benchmark from Data Center Alley's home team.

companies.name: Holder Construction
companies.tagline: The quiet giant of hyperscale construction — BD+C's #1 data-center contractor in 2023-24; Google's $2B Fort Wayne campus and EdgeCore's 450 MW Mesa build behind an NDA-heavy low profile.

companies.name: Huawei Digital Power
companies.tagline: The excluded benchmark — #1 in prefab modular DCs and PV inverters, CNY 77.3B revenue; US-banned and EU-phasing-out, so its AIDC market is the Gulf and APAC.

companies.name: HyperStrong
companies.tagline: China's grid-side integration specialist — HyperBlock M 12.8 MWh, a ≥200 GWh CATL pact plus 60 GWh sodium, and ~10 GWh of 2026 overseas orders with the Americas slice described as data-center storage.

companies.name: Infineon Technologies
companies.tagline: The silicon layer of the 800 VDC chain — SiC, GaN and silicon from the solid-state transformer to the point of load; Gartner’s “company to beat” in AI data-centre power semiconductors, and one of fourteen NVIDIA silicon partners rather than a sole source.

companies.name: IREN
companies.tagline: The vertically integrated pivot — 5 GW secured power, Microsoft's $9.7B GB300 contract delivered on time, NVIDIA $3.4B + 5 GW DSX; ClusterMAX says Underperforming, the Street says $80.

companies.name: Jinko
companies.tagline: #1 module shipper absorbing its first loss in 12 years — storage (SunTera G3) is designated the second growth engine; ~246% US tariff exposure.

companies.name: Jupiter Power
companies.tagline: Hithium's biggest disclosed US customer — 3 GWh safe-harbored (2024), prospectus-named, and the 2.8 GWh Trimount design win — while its own channels stay silent and message domestic content. BlackRock-owned, ~8.8 GWh op/UC/contracted.

companies.name: Key Capture Energy
companies.tagline: The NYISO first-mover in play — Sungrow-built fleet, Powin scar tissue, zero Korean cells despite SK ownership, open LIPA/NYSERDA/Michigan procurement windows, and an unresolved sale process (Nomura).

companies.name: Kiewit
companies.tagline: The power picks-and-shovels of the AI boom — ~11 GW of gas EPC (Homer City 4.5 GW), completed HVDC (CHPE), and the Oklo SMR constructor seat; employee-owned at ENR #4.

companies.name: Lambda
companies.tagline: The Superintelligence Cloud — Microsoft multibillion + NVIDIA leaseback anchors, $5.9B Series E, first IG-rated private-neocloud term loan; H2 2026 IPO window.

companies.name: LG Energy Solution
companies.tagline: ESS pivot underway — 140 GWh backlog and the Tesla Megapack LFP award; we assess AMPC dependence as the profitability watch item.

companies.name: Lightsource bp
companies.tagline: The second verified Hithium customer — 640 MWh at Woolooga, Australia only; FEOC-clean First Solar in the US, Gotion won the next battery, and bp is reportedly selling the whole platform to a Kuwait-backed consortium.

companies.name: LITEON
companies.tagline: #2 in AI server power with the BBU franchise — shipments ~30x in 2025; 800V rack mass production Q1 2027, a step behind Delta, ASIC customers first.

companies.name: LS Energy Solutions
companies.tagline: The quiet Korean-owned option — ex-Parker Hannifin PCS heritage, Korean tier-1 cells, the Big Rock 200 MW/400 MWh flagship, and the cleanest FEOC story in the US mid-tier that nobody markets.

companies.name: Mainspring Energy
companies.tagline: Linear-generator maker (250 kW units, 46% LHV, <1.5 ppm NOx no SCR) — OBBBA's flat 30% ITC winner, ~$1B AIDC pipeline, exploring IPO under ex-Cummins CEO Linebarger

companies.name: MasTec
companies.tagline: The AIDC-committed diversifier — #1-class wind constructor (Wanzek/IEA), record $21.4B backlog, twice-documented Sungrow pairings, and a full data-center pivot: turnkey CM, $1.65B Superior electrical buy, >$1B hyperscaler pursuits.

companies.name: McCarthy
companies.tagline: 162-year-old, 100% employee-owned national builder: 418 MW of data centres delivered against 2 GW+ in preconstruction, and an ENR Top 400 rank that slipped 20 → 22 in the data-centre year.

companies.name: Megmeet
companies.tagline: Power-electronics platform converting to AI data-center power — the only mainland vendor NVIDIA named for GB200; the H1 2026 report is the test.

companies.name: Meta
companies.tagline: $130–145B capex and multi-GW self-build (Hyperion 5 GW) — utility-side BESS posture via tolled projects; financing shifted to SPV debt.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.tagline: RPO $678B and a nuclear-heavy portfolio (TMI restart 2027) — we assess BESS as the notable gap; Fairwater designs drop UPS entirely.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Electric
companies.tagline: Japanese electrical conglomerate whose large static UPS, transformers and gas-insulated switchgear sit on both sides of a data-center service entrance

companies.name: Mitsubishi Power
companies.tagline: The third heavy-duty gas turbine OEM — a brand of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, with 35 GW of large-frame backlog and a two-tier data-center bridge-power offer
companies.hq: Yokohama, Japan; Americas in Lake Mary, Florida

companies.name: Mortenson
companies.tagline: The power-and-shell contractor — top-10 ENR builder pairing 11 GW of data centers with 47.8 GW wind / 17 GW solar / 45 GWh storage EPC and gigawatt-class substations.

companies.name: Narada Power
companies.tagline: The distressed backup-power incumbent — #2 in DC/base-station batteries with GWh-scale semi-solid firsts, now under ST designation and a creditor reorganization petition; counterparty risk is the headline.

companies.name: Nebius
companies.tagline: CoreWeave's most direct challenger — ARR $3B (+56% QoQ), >$40B Microsoft/Meta backlog, 5 GW contracted-power target; ClusterMAX Gold; Vineland permits are the live risk.

companies.name: NextEra Energy Resources
companies.tagline: The market-maker — ~5.2 GW operating storage, a 95 GW storage pipeline, domestic supply locked through 2029 at 1.5x, and the defining AIDC franchise (Google campuses, Meta ESAs, Duane Arnold, the $67B Dominion merger).

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.tagline: The demand engine — sets rack-power architecture (800 VDC; 120 kW to 1 MW racks) and names its power-chain vendors; FY2026 revenue $215.9B.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.tagline: Pre-commercial SMR developer building a 75 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor at Idaho under DOE authorization, not an NRC licence; ~$3.0B raised against a non-binding order book.

companies.name: ON.energy
companies.tagline: BESS-based medium-voltage AI UPS™ pioneer — 5 GW Crusoe deployment, FEOC-clean US stack (cells unnamed); direct category competitor to Hithium's ∞Power AIDC line

companies.name: Oncor Electric Delivery
companies.tagline: The largest pure-play wires utility in the United States and the gate every gigawatt of North Texas data-center load must pass through — 298 GW of interconnection requests against a 31 GW peak, of which 44 GW cleared into ERCOT's Batch Zero and only ~8 GW is energized, a $47.5B plan doubling rate base to ~$69B by 2030, the first four 765 kV certificate applications in Texas history, and a governor's audit plus a lieutenant governor's objection now sitting on both.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.tagline: Anchor demand — ~$1.4T / ~30 GW committed against ~0.3 GW operational; the circular-financing debate is, in large part, the OpenAI-solvency debate.

companies.name: Oracle
companies.tagline: The AI-compute landlord — RPO $638B, roughly half attributed to OpenAI; a per-site power menu from gensets to Bloom fuel cells; FCF -$23.7B, funded on credit.

companies.name: Panasonic
companies.tagline: Incumbent BBU cell supplier converting EV capacity to data-center demand — ¥800B FY2029 energy target; Tesla concentration is the exposure.

companies.name: Piller Power Systems
companies.tagline: The rotary, diesel-rotary and flywheel UPS maker whose SHIELDX kinetic stabilizer now ships inside every Bergen Engines behind-the-meter AI plant — more than 3 GW signed by mid-2026 after a decade absent from hyperscale UPS; the constraint is the Osterode factory, going from ~100 to ~400 large systems a year by end-2027.

companies.name: Plus Power
companies.tagline: The tolling franchise — 1,650 MW/4,150 MWh across 5 states, dual-sourced Tesla + Sungrow (330+ PowerTitan containers), no public FEOC posture, and Sierra Estrella marketed as grid support for a 240 MW hyperscale campus.

companies.name: Powell Industries
companies.tagline: Houston engineer-to-order medium-voltage switchgear and factory-built power rooms, re-rated by a >$400M behind-the-meter data-center order

companies.name: Prevalon Energy
companies.tagline: Mitsubishi Power's storage spin-out turned Nextpower subsidiary — HD5 blocks and the Hybrid Power Stabilizer behind a claimed 1.3 GW of hyperscaler contracts, FEOC-armored by a 10 GWh AESC/Fixx domestic-cell deal.

companies.name: Primoris
companies.tagline: The 'outside-the-walls' AI contractor — #4 US solar EPC, Meta Nebraska and Crusoe gas power, record $13.9B backlog; 2026's guidance collapse made it a project-controls turnaround story.

companies.name: ProEnergy
companies.tagline: Refurb-jet-core aeroderivative supplier (PE6000, 48 MW) — >1.65 GW of AIDC turbine orders incl. Crusoe 650 MW on 2027 delivery; ECP-owned, no BESS offering

companies.name: QTS Data Centers
companies.tagline: Blackstone's $60B growth machine — leased capacity 14× since the take-private, 3 GW+ live with a $30B pre-leased pipeline stamped from the water-free Freedom design; the $4.6B Baa2 green bond marked the wholesale sector's IG debut.

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.tagline: #1 US electrical contractor at 3.7x the runner-up — $53.4B backlog, DC entry via Cupertino/Dynamic; doubling its own transformer capacity by 2028.

companies.name: Rehlko
companies.tagline: Formerly Kohler Energy; the only gen-set OEM that also builds a three-phase static UPS and MV paralleling switchgear

companies.name: Rolls-Royce Power Systems
companies.tagline: The mtu brand: diesel and gas gen-sets, a diesel-rotary UPS, grid-scale batteries and modular gas power plants

companies.name: Rosendin
companies.tagline: #2 US electrical contractor (ESOP, $5.6B revenue) — 15+ GW of data-center power built; BESSUPS with FlexGen moves BESS inside the fence.

companies.name: Samsung C&T
companies.tagline: The third Hithium prospectus reference — a ~10 GWh E&C cooperation agreement still unconverted after 19 months, a 20 GW US develop-and-sell platform whose buyers pick the batteries, and a fast-compounding AIDC axis (Stargate Korea, floating DCs).

companies.name: Samsung SDI
companies.tagline: First profit in seven quarters on UPS/BBU demand — SBB 2.0 and a world-first UL large-scale fire test; US LFP conversion lands October 2026.

companies.name: Schneider Electric
companies.tagline: Shared #1 in DC physical infrastructure — the NVIDIA reference-design franchise; a two-speed portfolio carried by triple-digit data-center demand.

companies.name: Siemens Energy
companies.tagline: Turbines plus grid from one book — €162B backlog, Gas Services book-to-bill 2.65, the Eaton 500 MW SGT-800 block; rebranding to Omterra late 2026.

companies.name: Sinexcel
companies.tagline: Modular power electronics — overseas storage PCS is the margin engine; EV charging and power quality lines; AIDC power pre-revenue.

companies.name: SOLV Energy
companies.tagline: The pure-play benchmark — #2 US BESS builder 2024 (4.6 GWh), >21 GW built, the largest solar O&M fleet (~22 GW), a Feb 2026 Nasdaq IPO (MWH), and owner-furnished Tesla on every flagship; 'actively exploring storage for data centers.'

companies.name: Southern Company
companies.tagline: The Southeast's regulated AI-load gatekeeper with no RTO above it and an elected commission beneath it — 17 GW of contracted large load at July 2026 against a 75 GW-plus prospective pipeline it does not count, 9,885 MW certified by the Georgia PSC in one December 2025 order under a base-rate freeze through 2028 and a 2029–2031 shareholder backstop, an $81B plan backed by $26.5B of DOE loan guarantees, and the Vogtle overrun as its risk memory.

companies.name: STACK Infrastructure
companies.tagline: Blue Owl's named-tenant build engine — developer-owner of all three campuses in Amazon's $18B Louisiana program plus the 1 GW+ Stargate 'Project Jupiter'; 13 GW stated pipeline across three ring-fenced regions, ten ABS series since 2019, a reported $30B+ APAC sale in motion.

companies.name: Sungrow
companies.tagline: PV inverters and PowerTitan BESS — holds both 2026 Wood Mackenzie #1 rankings; we assess ESS is now the profit center.

companies.name: Sunwoda
companies.tagline: The fastest riser of the Chinese top ten — first to a million 684 Ah cells, ~#9 integrator at 25.6 GWh (+188%), US-relevant only through its AIDC backup/BBU lane.

companies.name: Switch
companies.tagline: Patent-moated Tier 5 landlord of the AI-factory era — five US Prime campuses, 2 MW-per-rack EVO halls, a 12 GW Oklo nuclear option and $24B raised since 2024; a confidential S-1 is filed at a reported $50–80B.

companies.name: TeraWulf
companies.tagline: The power landlord of AI — 839 MW leased / ~$27B contracted incl. the 401 MW Anthropic lease; Google backstops $4.5B of Fluidstack paper for ~14% of the equity.

companies.name: Terra-Gen
companies.tagline: The FEOC pivot case study — world's largest single BESS site (E&S, 3.3 GWh on LG/Samsung/BYD) then an 8 GWh, ~$1.43B US-made LG Vertech lock through 2029; Masdar/Igneo-owned with a 1 GWh NY build ahead.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.tagline: Megapack, Powerwall, and Autobidder — leading Western integrator; Brookshire ramp and Megapack 3 deliveries are the watch items.

companies.name: Trane Technologies
companies.tagline: $21.3B applied-HVAC maker whose backlog hit $12.1B (+70%) on data-centre chiller demand — with LiquidStack and Stellar Energy bought in 2026 and no data-centre revenue disclosed.

companies.name: Trina Storage
companies.tagline: Elementa 2 Pro/3 and grid-forming Electra from the solar major — exited T1 Energy to ~10%, no US manufacturing, betting bankability over volume in Europe and Asia.

companies.name: Turner Construction
companies.tagline: ENR's #1 US contractor six years running — data-center revenue tripling toward a $20B-by-2030 target on Meta, CoreWeave, and Stargate mega-campuses; SourceBlue buys the gear.

companies.name: Vantage Data Centers
companies.tagline: The giga-scale Stargate landlord — 41 campuses / ~9 GW on five continents, 1.4 GW Frontier + 902 MW Lighthouse for Oracle/OpenAI behind a record $38B loan; invented the data-center ABS, now reportedly exploring a ~$100B IPO.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.tagline: The pure-play AI-DC power and cooling benchmark — $15B backlog, Dell'Oro co-#1 with Schneider; the Q2 revenue miss made execution the live question.

companies.name: Vicor
companies.tagline: Point-of-load and bus-converter silicon for the 48 V and 800 V AI rack — factorized power, current multipliers and vertical power delivery from one Andover ChiP fab; a 2025 ITC exclusion order over its bus-converter patents took royalties to 21% of Q2 2026 revenue, a second ITC case runs to 2027, and it is absent from every NVIDIA 800 VDC partner list.

companies.name: VoltaGrid
companies.tagline: Volume leader of behind-the-meter AIDC gas power — 2.3 GW Oracle/OpenAI, >1 GW Vantage; Blackstone/Halliburton $1B equity, $5B debt; the defining FEOC-immune adjacent competitor

companies.name: Wärtsilä
companies.tagline: Quantum BESS and GEMS moving into a 50/50 RCT JV (Q3 2026); the retained engine business independently monetizes data-center power.

companies.name: xAI
companies.tagline: The extreme case in behind-the-fence power — ~1 GW Colossus on self-built gas + the largest Megapack fleet; now inside SpaceX, monetized by Anthropic at $15B/yr.

companies.name: Xcel Energy
companies.tagline: The eight-state utility whose AI-load story is gated by commissions rather than demand — ~2 GW contracted against a 20 GW-plus pipeline, one approved large-load tariff (Minnesota) and two pending (Colorado, Wisconsin), a 1,900 MW Google package recovered through a customer-specific Clean Energy Accelerator Charge, turbines and wind reserved with GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and NextEra before the tariffs were decided, and a Smokehouse Creek liability the company says it cannot cap.

companies.name: Zhonhen Electric
companies.tagline: China's data-center HVDC leader — #1 at 31% share, Alibaba's Panama co-developer, now pushing 800V overseas via Enervell/SuperX while CATL buys 49% of its holdco.

companies.name: DNV
companies.tagline: Norwegian foundation-owned assurance and risk-management group (NOK 43.9bn revenue, 2025) whose Energy Systems arm writes the recommended practices and independent-engineer reports that make batteries and grids bankable — and runs the labs the data comes from.

companies.name: Sargent & Lundy
companies.tagline: Chicago power-engineering firm since 1891, privately owned and led by engineers, working as owner's engineer, independent engineer and engineer of record on nuclear restarts, SMRs, gas plants, grid and data-centre campus power — fee-for-service, no equity, no construction.

companies.name: CoolIT Systems
companies.tagline: Calgary direct-liquid-cooling specialist — cold plates, rack manifolds and 80 kW to 2 MW CDUs on NVIDIA's recommended-vendor list — bought by Ecolab for about USD 4.75bn (closed July 2026) after three years under KKR and Mubadala.

companies.name: Fluidstack
companies.tagline: Tenant-of-record on ~1.4 GW of Anthropic-bound leases at TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8 and Meridian Arc — bankable only through Google's backstops and penny warrants; owns one campus (Abernathy, July 2026) and USD 2.6bn of equity against ~USD 27bn of rent.

companies.name: Nscale
companies.tagline: Microsoft-anchored European neocloud that owns its ground — Glomfjord and Narvik hydro, the 2 GW Caterpillar-powered Monarch campus — ~200,000 GB300 + 96,000 Rubin contracted, a reported USD 45bn Anthropic deal after Microsoft walked, USD 3.7bn equity and USD 6.1bn debt against ~USD 100M quarterly revenue.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.tagline: The compute buyer — up to 5 GW of Trainium, 'well over a gigawatt' of TPUs then multi-GW from 2027, USD 30bn of Azure, all of Colossus 1, a 401 MW direct lease, a 470 MW gas order and reported USD 45bn/USD 35bn neocloud contracts, on run-rate revenue of USD 47bn and a USD 965bn Series H ahead of an IPO.

companies.name: Aypa Power
companies.tagline: Blackstone-owned standalone battery-storage platform under a signed, pending sale to Brookfield — about 6.5 GW operating, under construction and contracted, 95% contracted per the buyer

companies.name: Spearmint Energy
companies.tagline: Founder-led merchant BESS developer-owner — 350 MW / 700 MWh operating in ERCOT plus 300 MW under construction, financed on private credit, tax equity and credit transfer with no named offtaker

companies.name: Intersect
companies.tagline: Google-owned since March 2026 (USD 4.75bn plus debt) — the co-located energy-park developer behind the Quantum and Meitner Texas campuses; its grid-tied fleet was carved out as IPX Power

companies.name: Invenergy
companies.tagline: Chicago's privately held developer-operator — #2 US pipeline behind NextEra, CDPQ- and Blackstone-owned, storage in Arizona, gas plants for utilities' data-centre load, Grain Belt Express

companies.name: GridStor
companies.tagline: Goldman Sachs Asset Management-owned standalone-storage owner — contracted batteries in California, Texas and Arizona, five late-stage acquisitions in eighteen months

companies.name: Available Power
companies.tagline: Texas develop-and-sell developer of 9.9 MW distribution-connected batteries, a unit of Available Infrastructure; no operating fleet on the record since the parent's 2025 edge-AI pivot

companies.name: esVolta
companies.tagline: Generate Capital-owned standalone-storage owner in a sale process — hedged-and-merchant batteries in ERCOT, resource-adequacy batteries in CAISO, a 25 GWh pipeline into Arizona and New Mexico

companies.name: Strata Clean Energy
companies.tagline: Founder-owned developer-EPC-owner that wins utility tolls and sells the battery with the contract attached — Scatter Wash to CIP, White Tank to GridStor — while keeping about 1 GW of owned solar

companies.name: Hunt Energy Network
companies.tagline: Hunt-family-owned, Manulife-funded merchant owner-trader of 32 distribution-connected 9.9 MW batteries plus a 100 MW transmission battery in ERCOT, dispatched by its own QSE

companies.name: Talen Energy
companies.tagline: The co-location precedent that failed and the contract that replaced it — FERC rejected the behind-the-meter Susquehanna arrangement in November 2024, and the 1,920 MW Amazon deal that followed is an ordinary front-of-the-meter retail supply needing no FERC approval; 15.7 GW of PJM generation anchored by 90 percent of one nuclear station, rebuilt on $9.7 billion of debt.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.tagline: The integrated merchant that became a nuclear contracting story — 3.8 GW of six reactors sold to Amazon and Meta on twenty-year agreements, a five-million-customer retail book that hedges 43,641 MW of generation, and a battery fleet cut from 1,024 MW to 624 MW by the Moss Landing fire; nothing signed at any gas site.

companies.name: NRG Energy
companies.tagline: A retail company that owns power plants — 96 percent of revenue from eight million customers, a fleet doubled to 25 GW by the closed LS Power acquisition, 6 GW of demand response through CPower, and the only large merchant with no named hyperscaler: its 1.2 GW Texas project is 'aligned on principal commercial terms', not signed.
